text:
It is truly heartwarming to witness the modern educational system’s commitment to replacing academic rigor with interpretive dance. Who needs to understand the molecular structure of paraffin wax when you can simply belt out a high note about it? The candle, that humble beacon of light, is no longer a source of illumination but a prop for a spontaneous Broadway number.

In this brave new world, the primary material of a candle is no longer wax, wick, or flame. It is, unequivocally, *drama*. Why bother with the tedious details of hydrocarbons when you can solve the mystery of why the light flickers by engaging in a choreographed battle of the bands? The wick is merely a microphone stand, and the melting wax is just the tears of joy shed by the audience as they realize that complex chemical reactions are best understood through the universal language of jazz hands.

After all, if you can’t out-dance your problems, are you even trying? The candle doesn’t burn; it performs. And if you look closely, you’ll see that the "primary material" is actually just pure, unadulterated irony, solidified into a shape that begs to be sung about in a major key.
